title: Discriminant Dungeon
description: Use b²-4ac and completing the square to escape the quadratic maze.

concepts.def: ax²+bx+c=0 with a≠0 is the standard quadratic.
Δ = b²-4ac tells you the nature of roots.
If b²-4ac > 0 the quadratic has two distinct real roots.
If b²-4ac = 0 there is one repeated real root.
If b²-4ac < 0 there are no real solutions (complex pair).
x²+bx+c = (x+b/2)² + c - (b/2)² gives min/max and roots.

mcqs.q: If the discriminant of a quadratic is negative, what does it tell you about real roots?
options: x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
There are no real roots — the graph does not cross the x-axis.
There are infinitely many roots.
There is one repeated root — the curve just touches the x-axis.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
The square root of x (the positive root when x is positive).
x^(1/2) means x divided by 2 — half of x.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.

mcqs.q: What is the value of x^0 (for x not equal to zero)?
options: x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
x^0 equals 0 because raising something to the zero gives nothing.
1 — any non-zero number to the power of zero equals 1.
There are infinitely many roots.
